analysis:
The PR adds scoped stop-string matching for GPT-OSS so that stops match only inside the Harmony final message. In EngineV2Bridge+StopSequence.swift (head lines 14-32), the bridge passes its stopStringScope to the static matcher. When a scope is set, the matcher replays StopHoldback over the decoded text and reports the first candidate that is a prefix of the tail after the emitted text. Otherwise the original earliest-position scan is unchanged (head 33-58). In EngineV2Bridge+Submission.swift (head 249-250), stopStringScope is plumbed into the CBv2Request.

Security relevance is limited to output-filtering correctness. Harmony analysis is hidden reasoning, so scoping stops to the final channel reduces truncation driven by reasoning text. No encryption, attestation, authorization, cache-salt or prefix-cache (T-041) paths are touched. A wrong reported stop label affects only finish metadata, not plaintext exposure (T-008). Whether withheld analysis text could leak through the stop-reporting path depends on StopHoldback and ModelEOSPolicy.stopStringScope, which live in the mlx-swift-lm submodule and are not visible here. If no candidate matches the tail, the matcher returns nil, a benign outcome.

Three submodule pins changed with no visible diff: libs/mlx 31f550a->72dffa2, libs/mlx-swift 4926d3d->c633d22 and libs/mlx-swift-lm aee6ebb->2beb401. These pins bring in inference/runtime code (TB-007, T-028, T-010, T-041 engine paths) that this pass cannot review. That is a coverage limit, not evidence the code is safe. Integration should confirm that the StopHoldback scope semantics and the submodule changes do not alter cache-salt plumbing or the CBv2Request cacheSalt or reasoning withholding.

The visible portion of docs/architecture/inference.md (head 2424-2961) is documentation; its one changed line (1846) documents the stop scope.
